forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Bromley projects a £62.4m schools deficit and a £35.5m reserves drawdown to balance 2026/27
news_drafts.lead:
Bromley Council's November budget monitoring report estimates a dedicated schools grant (DSG) deficit of £62.403m at the end of 2026/27. The figure is a projected in-year overspend of £22.339m added to £39.979m carried forward from 2025/26. The DSG is the government grant that funds schools; the council's overspend on it sits in the part of the grant for special educational needs. Officers are preparing a recovery plan with the Department for Education, which the paper says will be considered in due course.

The government has confirmed a High Needs Stability Grant for Bromley of £35.981m, covering 90% of the cumulative DSG deficit to 2025/26. The council expects about £36m to be received in 2026/27 and assumes the same 90% proportion for 2026/27 and 2027/28 in its updated forecast. Separately, the paper says the estimated drawdown from reserves needed to balance the 2026/27 budget "increases from £25,422k to £33,181k". A further £2.3m drawdown, taking the total to £35.481m, would be needed to meet the balance remaining after the grant.

On staffing, the Executive paper reports permanent recruitment in children's social care at 94%, and says ten additional education, health and care plan officers have been recruited. Agency workers remaining in the special educational needs and disabilities service are due to leave by mid-January 2027.

news_drafts.headline: Bromley's risk register lists uncertain government support for schools deficit from 2026/27
news_drafts.lead:
Bromley Council's finance risk register records uncertainty over how much government support it will receive from 2026/27 towards a deficit on the dedicated schools grant, the government grant that funds schools, where a deficit is usually an overspend on support for children with special needs. The register is Appendix D to papers for the Executive, Resources and Contracts Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee, which meets on 23 November 2026.

The register lists the uncertainty as a cause of its risk on government reforms and new burdens. It describes the position as "Uncertainty on level of Government support for DSG deficit from 2026/27 (90% was funded up to 2025/26)".

The register gives that risk a current rating of 12 and a target rating of 9. Both are scored as likelihood multiplied by impact. The papers do not give a figure for the deficit.

news_drafts.headline: Bromley forecasts £22.4m high-needs overspend for 2026/27; 90% SEND deficit write-off awaited
news_drafts.lead:
Bromley Council forecasts a £22.4m overspend for 2026/27 on its dedicated schools grant (DSG), the government grant that funds schools, according to papers for the Children, Education and Families committee on 18 November. The overspend is mainly in high needs, the part that funds special educational needs and disabilities. The papers also say a government write-off of 90% of historic SEND deficits would, on current figures, remove £36.0m of Bromley's deficit and leave £4.0m at the end of 2025/26.

The write-off depends on a "local SEND reform plan", which Bromley submitted to the Department for Education in June 2026. The paper says the allocation, and any drawdown in November 2026, are still awaited. The council carried forward a DSG deficit of £40.0m from 2025/26 and estimates its DSG reserve at £62.3m by the end of 2026/27. Of this year's amount, £16.5m is already budgeted. The paper identifies a further £5.8m that it says will be met from reserves unless ongoing funding is found, and it says the specific reserves have not yet been identified. It describes the position as "financially unsustainable" in the medium to longer term. Education, health and care plans numbered 5,070 in September 2026, 46 above the budget profile of 5,024, against 27 above in April.

On SEND transport, the risk register says independent travel training and personal transport budgets are "successfully driving down costs". The committee approved in June 2026 a procurement through an Open Framework, with the contract starting in September 2027.

findings.headline: 29 young people have been moved into accommodation with an estimated saving of c£400k.
findings.detail: The Director of Children's Services says the housing task force has moved 29 young people, with no tenancy disruptions reported. The saving is described as estimated.
findings.matters: A quantified move-on saving from the housing service into the children's budget is a cross-departmental saving other councils may replicate.
findings.figures: 29 young people moved; estimated saving c£400k.
findings.quote: have successfully moved 29 young people with an estimated savings of c£400k

findings.headline: Experts at Hand is expected to go live in March 2027.
findings.detail: The Director of Children's Services states the expected go-live date for the Experts at Hand model, which is intended to bring specialist expertise closer to schools and reduce escalation into statutory provision.
findings.matters: A dated go-live for a major SEND redesign gives peers and lenders a milestone to test the council's claimed reduction in escalation.
findings.quote: We are expecting the Expert at Hand Model to go live in March 2027

findings.headline: Planning fee income is reported to have reduced significantly in recent years due to fewer applications.
findings.detail: The Director of Housing, Planning and Regeneration says whilst fee income has risen this year, the level of applications is not expected in the medium to longer term. Planning is reported at no variation to budget.
findings.matters: Fee income falling below delivery cost is a structural issue for planning services at councils across England, and the paper states the medium-term expectation.
findings.figures: Planning portfolio variation £0; no quantified fee shortfall in the paper.
findings.quote: Planning fee income reduced significantly in recent years due to a decrease in the number of

findings.headline: Environment & Community is projected at a £170k overspend in Arboriculture Management.
findings.detail: The paper says the demand for essential tree services is forecasting an overspend, which will be reviewed again for Q3. Waste disposal is projected in line with budget, while parking income may fall below budget as compliance rises.
findings.matters: Parking income moving with compliance is a specific point of income risk that other authorities running moving-traffic enforcement will also recognise.
findings.figures: Arboriculture Management variation £170k; Environment & Community total variation £170k.
findings.quote: the demand for essential services is forecasting a projected overspend

findings.headline: Recruitment of permanent children's social care staff is reported at 94%, with agency workers due to leave the SEND service by mid-January 2027.
findings.detail: The Director says permanent staff recruitment has reduced agency spend, while some agency staff still contribute to overspend awaiting HR processes. Ten additional EHCP officers have been recruited.
findings.matters: Agency cost reduction and permanent recruitment rates are workforce measures that determine how far an overspend recurs in the next year.
findings.figures: Permanent staff recruitment 94%; 10 additional EHCP officers; remaining EHCP agency workers to leave by mid-January 2027.
findings.quote: The continued progress in recruiting permanent staff (94%)
